To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the more stakeholders participate during the evaluation of a small program, the more likely it is that the evaluation will be valid and useful, and (2) the more the evaluator interacts with stakeholders during the study, the more valid and useful the study will be.
stakeholder participation during the evaluation of education programs can help achieve the raison d'etre of both collaborative and non-collative evaluations.

(a) the extent of stakeholder participation during evaluation can vary from none to extensive, and (b) the extent to which stakeholders participate during an evaluation should depend on whether the purpose of the study is primarily to enhance the use of evaluation results or to enhance the validity of findings.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the extent to which stakeholder participation can help ensure evaluation validity in both collaborative and non-collabortive evaluations.
the question of how to achieve the best possible evaluation for the purpose of generating valid, useful findings.
the extent to which the participation of stakeholders during evaluation can help ensure the validity of findings and enhance the use of evaluation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the gap between collaborative and non-collative evaluations is not so wide that they cannot be bridged.

the gap between collaborative and non-collative evaluations can be bridged by the application of stakeholder participation theories and methods for the purpose of ensuring the validity of evaluation findings.
the gap between collaborative and non-collative evaluations can be bridged by using the same theories and methods to enhance both the use of evaluation and the validity of evaluations.

, for the purpose of helping ensure validity, stakeholder participation can be used in a variety of ways and at a variety of points in an evaluation.
